papers.title: Effects of Void Array Orientation on Compressive Properties of Cellular Structures
papers.abstract: Additively manufactured cellular materials enable customized structural implants with superior osseointegration potential and mechanical properties better matched to bone. In this investigation, the compression response of Ti–6Al–4V alloy cellular materials comprising a simple cubic array of 2.00 mm diameter spherical voids with a 1.90 mm inter‐void spacing are studied. Finite element analysis (FEA) shows that the lattice exhibited cubic symmetry with values for Young's modulus (E), Poisson's ratio, and shear modulus in the range of 28.5–29.5 GPa, 0.18–0.20, and 5.4–6.0 GPa, respectively. Compression tests carried out on cylinders with the same cellular structure fabricated by selective laser melting also show a strong dependence of elastic and plastic properties on orientation. Compression normal to the {100} plane of the simple cubic cell gives the highest E and strength, while compression normal to the {110} and {111} planes give lower values. The experimental E values for the {100} and {111} orientations show good agreement with the FEA results, but the {110} orientation shows lower values of E compared to the FEA predictions. Ultimate compressive failure of the cylinders occurred by gross slip along the {100} planes of the void array – coinciding with the slip planes for the simple cubic system.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了SLM制造的多孔Ti-6Al-4V结构的压缩性能与取向依赖性，有助于理解刚度匹配，但未涉及疲劳、表面粗糙度或骨整合。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not cover fatigue testing, surface roughness characterization, or osseointegration assessment, which are critical for biomedical implant validation.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究Ti-6Al-4V多孔结构压缩性能的取向依赖性，以匹配骨骼刚度。
summary_zh.method: 通过FEA和SLM制造样品的压缩实验分析简单立方空隙阵列的取向效应。
summary_zh.result: {100}取向弹性模量和强度最高，{110}和{111}较低，失效沿{100}晶面滑移。
summary_zh.validation: 压缩实验结果与FEA预测在{100}和{111}取向吻合良好。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the orientation-dependent compressive properties of Ti-6Al-4V cellular structures with simple cubic void arrays for potential biomedical implant applications.
summary_en.method: Finite element analysis and experimental compression tests were conducted on selective laser melted cylinders with a simple cubic array of spherical voids to examine orientation effects.
summary_en.result: Compression normal to the {100} plane yielded the highest elastic modulus and strength, while normal to {110} and {111} gave lower values; failure occurred by gross slip along {100} planes.
summary_en.validation: Experimental elastic moduli for {100} and {111} orientations agreed well with FEA predictions, though {110} showed lower experimental values.
